info.name: UCC API Collection
info.description: Collection of all API endpoints for UCC microservices

request.description: Dedicated super_admin login — the shared /login endpoint rejects this role.

Public self-registration — patient only. Any `role` sent is ignored; staff accounts can only be created by a super_admin (see Super Admin Service > Users). Creates the account as `pending_verification` and emails/texts an OTP — returns `{ userId, otpSentVia }`, no tokens. Run Verify OTP (Registration) next to activate the account.
Subject to a resend cooldown (integrations.otp.resendCooldownSeconds, default 60s). purpose is also "password_reset" for the forgot-password flow.

Codes are never returned by the API — read it from wherever notification-service actually delivered it (real inbox/phone once Super Admin > Integrations has real SendGrid/Twilio creds, or the notification-service console log for a mock send), then set {{otp_code}} before running this. On success, activates the account and returns tokens (saved to patient_token/patient_refresh_token).
Dedicated patient login — the shared /login endpoint rejects this role. Returns 403 while the account is still pending_verification — run Verify OTP (Registration) first.

Precursor to Forgot Password. identifier can be an email or a phone number. Returns which delivery channels exist for the account (masked email/phone) so the client can render a "send code via email / sms" choice. Returns an empty options array (200) for an unknown identifier — no user enumeration.
identifier can be an email or a phone number. Always returns 200 with a generic message — never reveals whether the account exists.
Opens a short 10-minute window for Reset Password. Does not issue tokens.
Requires a successful Verify OTP (Password Reset) first — otherwise 400. Revokes all existing refresh tokens on success.

item.name: Appointment Booking
item.description: Guest-first appointment booking wizard, collapsed into two calls: (1) Booking API — consultation option → date/time + doctor → slot + intake + consents in one request; (2) Payment & Confirmation API — Stripe pre-auth (captured when the visit starts) whose response already carries the confirmed booking. Registered patients send the same requests with a Bearer token and only need the appointment details + intake. Without STRIPE_SECRET_KEY the billing service uses a mock gateway, so the flow runs end-to-end locally.

request.description: Public catalog: Telehealth $75, In-office $100, Home visit $175.

exec: pm.test('201 held with intake complete', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(201); const b = pm.response.json().booking; pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('held'); pm.expect(b.intakeStatus).to.eql('complete'); });

request.description: Combines the old hold + intake calls. Reserves the slot for 10 minutes with intake answers and consents attached. Guests must send guest.email + persons + the consent trio (treatment, data_privacy, telehealth) in intake.consents.

item.name: 5. Pay & Confirm — Stripe pre-auth (charged when visit starts)

request.description: Combines the old pay + get-confirmation calls. Creates a manual-capture Stripe PaymentIntent via billing-service, confirms the booking, assigns the UCC number, opens the case, and returns the full confirmation payload ({ booking, case, payment, coordinatorId }) — no follow-up GET needed. Use pm.environment stripe_payment_method (pm_card_visa in test mode); the client normally sends a Stripe.js PaymentMethod id.
Registered patients only provide appointment details — identity comes from the token.

item.name: 2. Book Appointment (details + intake — no guest fields)

exec: pm.test('201 held for the account patient, intake complete', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(201); const b = pm.response.json().booking; pm.expect(b.guestFlag).to.eql(false); pm.expect(b.patientId).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(b.intakeStatus).to.eql('complete'); });

request.description: Combines the old hold + intake calls. Registered patients only need appointment details + intake — persons/guest come from the account, and only the consent trio is required for guests (registered patients can sign just what applies).
Prices are quoted USD and charged in COP at the day’s TRM.
Coordinator/physician captures the held funds when the visit starts.

item.name: Super Admin Service
item.description: All routes are super_admin-only (RBAC enforced server-side). superadmin-service proxies these to auth-service's internal admin API — Location/RoleConfig/PlatformSetting/AuditLog are owned by auth-service.

item.name: Integrations
item.description: Third-party API credentials (Stripe/Twilio/SendGrid/Google/Firebase), managed here instead of .env. Secret values (Stripe secretKey/webhookSecret, Twilio authToken, SendGrid apiKey, ...) are encrypted at rest and come back masked on GET (e.g. '••••1234'). Changes take effect immediately for notification-service/billing-service — no restart needed.

request.description: secretKey is live-validated against Stripe's API before saving; invalid keys are rejected with 400.
accountSid/authToken are live-validated against Twilio's Accounts API before saving.
apiKey comes back masked (e.g. 'SG.••••1234'); senderEmail is public so it's shown in full.
apiKey is live-validated against SendGrid's API before saving.

item.name: Users
item.description: Create accounts for any of the eight canonical roles. Only super_admin can call this — it's the sole way to create staff accounts (patients self-register instead, see Auth Service > Register).

request.description: Active immediately with credentialsVerified: true — the admin creating the account is the verification step.
Base fields only — same shape works for coordinator, office_manager, marketing, fulfillment, super_admin.
